stem: Which of the following is not a luminous object?
expl: A luminous object is one that produces its own light. Candle flame, electric lamp, and the Sun all emit their own light; hence they are luminous objects. The Moon does not produce its own light; it only reflects the sunlight. Therefore, it is a non-luminous object.

stem: Which of the following radiations has the highest energy per quantum?
expl: Photon energy is directly proportional to the wave frequency and inversely proportional to the wavelength. Thus, among the given options 200-280 nm radiation has the highest energy per quantum. Ultraviolet radiation contains sufficient energy per quantum to damage living cells. The ultraviolet spectrum is divided into UV-A (320- 400 nm) responsible for tanning the skin; UV-B (280-320 nm) responsible for skin cancer and vitamin D synthesis; and UV-C (below 280 nm), potentially the most harmful waveband but absorbed almost completely by molecular oxygen in the stratosphere.

expl: The human ear is most sensitive to sounds between 1000 and 5000 Hz. The human eye is most sensitive to yellowish- green colour. When fully light-adapted, the human eye features a wavelength response from around 380 to 700 nanometers, with a peak sensitivity at 555 nanometers (in the yellowish-green region of the visible light spectrum). The impression of sound heard by our ears persist in our mind for 1/10th of a second. If another sound is heard before 1/10 second is over, the impression of the two sound mixes up and our mind cannot differentiate among the two. Persistence of vision is a phenomenon of the human eye wherein the image formed on the retina is retained by the brain for 1/16th of a second. Hence, statement of option (b) is incorrect.

stem: The nature of radiation of light is-

options.label: c
options.text: Like both of wave and particle

options.label: d
options.text: Like neither of wave nor of particle

expl: The light has a dual nature, sometimes it behaves as wave and sometimes as particle. In the later part of the 19th century and in the beginning of 20th century, it was realized that black body radiation and the photoelectric effect can be understood only on the basis of particle model of light. Some experiments require light to be a wave, while others require light to be a particle. This led to the acceptance of dual nature of light. Quantum mechanics explains the duality of light by describing it as a wave-packet. A wave-packet refers to waves that may interact either as spatially localized, acting as particle, or interacting like waves.

stem: The formation of glittering colours in thin foam of soap is the result of which of the following phenomenon –

Now interference of refracted and reflected light gives soap foam glittering colour.

stem: The reason of mirage is :
expl: The mirage is caused by the refraction and total internal reflection of light at layers of air of different densities. In Desert areas, the successive upper layer is denser than those below there due to terrestrial heating. A ray of light coming from a distant object, like the top of a tree gets refracted from a denser to a rarer medium. Consequently, the refracted ray bends away from the normal until at a particular layer, the light is incident at an angle greater than the critical angle. At this stage, the incident ray suffers total internal reflection and enters the eyes of the observer. It appears as if an inverted image of the tree.

expl: The twinkling of a star is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight. The starlight, on entering the Earth's atmosphere, undergoes refraction continuously before it reaches the Earth. The atmospheric refraction occurs in a medium of gradually changing refractive index. Since the atmosphere bends starlight towards the normal, the apparent position of the star is slightly different from its actual position. The star appears slightly higher (above) than its actual position when viewed near the horizon. Since the stars are very distant, they approximate point-sized sources of light. As the path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the apparent position of the star fluctuates and the amount of starlight entering eye flickers – the star sometimes appear brighter and sometimes fainter, which is twinkling effect.

stem: When a soap film on the water is seen in the daytime, it shows beautiful colours. This phenomenon is due to:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The colours that we see when observing a soap film are caused by interference of light reflecting off of two nearby surfaces – the outer surface and the inner surface. Interference patterns are created when two reflected waves line up in phase or out of phase. White light is a mixture of all the wavelengths of the visible spectrum and the interference enhances some wavelengths and diminishes others, creating visible colours. The specific wavelengths that are enhanced or diminished are determined by the thickness of the film and its index of refraction.

stem: Suppose a rocketship is proceeding from the Earth at a speed of 2/10th the velocity of light. A light in the rocketship appears blue to the passengers on the ship. What colour would it appear to an observer on the Earth?
expl: To determine the color that would appear to an observer on the Earth, we use the following formula. ν = ± (λ – λ/λ) C Where λ = Prime wavelength λ = Virtual wavelength ν = Velocity of rocket C = Velocity of light Because the rocket is proceeding from the Earth, thus positive sign will be taken. Because the wavelength of blue colour lies between 450nm to 490 nm. Thus, the wavelength of the light would appear to an observer on the Earth has a range between 562.5 nm to 612.5 nm, which will be yellow-orange light.

stem: What will be the nature of image formed by a convex mirror when the position of object is between infinity and pole P of the mirror?
expl: When the position of object is between infinity and pole (P) of the convex mirror, then the image will be formed between the pole (P) and the focus (F) behind the mirror. The image thus formed is diminished, virtual and erect.

stem: Large number of thin strips of black paint are made on the surface of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm to catch the image of a white horse. The image will be:

When the lens has a large number of thin black strips on its surface, these strips will block or absorb some of the incident light. As a result, less light will reach the focal point and form the image. Hence, thin black strips on the surface of a convex lens will only reduce the intensity of the light but will not cast any shadow on the image, as it is quite thin. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem: As the diameter of objective lens of a telescope increases, the resolution of telescope :

options.label: b
options.text: Depends on focal length of lens

expl: Resolution or resolving power is the ability of a telescope to distinguish between two closely spaced objects. The objective lens is the primary lens in a refracting telescope that gathers light from a distant object. A larger objective lens gathers more light, which brightens the image and improves the contrast, making it easier to resolve details. With a larger objectives lens, the telescope can see smaller details and finer features in the image. The resolution of a telescope is limited by diffraction, a phenomenon where light waves bend around obstacles. A larger aperture (diameter) helps reduce the effects of diffraction, leading to sharper images. Thus, as the diameter of the objective lens of a telescope increases, its resolving power also increases, allowing it to distinguish finer details.

The water droplets act like small prisms. They refract and disperse the incident sunlight causing the white light to split in different colours and then reflect it internally and finally refract it again at multiple angles when it comes out of the raindrop.

stem: In which direction the rainbow is seen at 12 noon?

stem: Which of the following is responsible for production of shadow ?
expl: Shadows are formed when an opaque object obstructs the path of light, preventing it from reaching a surface or area behind the object. Light travels in straight lines, and when it encounters an opaque object, it cannot pass through, creating a dark region behind the object. The shape of the shadow is determined by the shape of the object blocking the light and the position of the light source relative to the object. Hence, rectilinear propagation of light is responsible for forming a shadow.

stem: The reason for a swimming pool to appear less deep than the actual depth is :
expl: A swimming pool appears less deep than its actual depth because light rays from the bottom of the pool are bent away from the normal as they pass from water into the air (denser to rarer medium). This phenomenon is called the refraction of light. Due to this the image of the bottom of the pool seems nearer to us and the pool appears less deep.

stem:
Assertion (A) : A stick is dipped in water in a slanting position. If observed sideways, the stick appears short and bent at the surface of the water.
Reason (R) : A light coming from the stick undergoes scattering from water molecules giving the stick a short and bent appearance.

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)

expl: When a stick is dipped in water in a slanting position, it appears short and bent at the surface of water. It is caused by the phenomenon of refraction of light. When you immerse a stick in water, you are actually putting and watching it from rarer medium to denser medium. When the rays of light pass from denser to rarer medium they refract and move away from the normal and reach the person's eye. Hence, stick appears to be bent and short when immersed in water due to refraction of light. Hence, (A) is true but (R) is false.

stem:

expl: Statement 1 is true. The coin will appear to be closer than it really is due to the refraction of light. In this case, the ray that is coming to the eyes is traveling from denser medium (water) to the rarer medium (air). The statement 2 is also true. If a person underwater looks at a coin above the water surface the coin will appear to be at a higher level than it really is also due to the refraction of light. In this case, the ray is travelling from the rarer medium to denser medium.

stem: To remove the defect of long sightedness one uses :
expl: Far-sightedness (hypermetropia) as it is medically termed is a vision condition in which distant object are usually seen clear, but near objects are not clearly visible. To remove this vision problem one should use a convex lens.

expl: We see the world around us because of the way our eyes bend (refract) light. The refractive or bending power of the cornea and humor is constant. However, that of the lens can be changed by changing its shape. That is by making it more or less convex so that light can be properly focused on the retina. The greater the lens convexity or bulge the more it bends the light. The flatter the lens, the less it bends that light.

stem: The change of focal length of an eye lens is caused by action of the :
expl: The eye lens is composed of a fibrous, jelly-like material. Its curvature can be modified to some extent by the ciliary muscles. The change in the curvature of the eye lens can thus change its focal length. When the muscles are relaxed, the lens becomes thin. Thus its focal length increases. This enables us to see distant objects clearly. When you are looking at objects closer to the eye, the ciliary muscles contract. This increases the curvature of the eye lens. The eye lens then becomes thicker. Consequently, the focal length of the eye lens decreases. This enables us to see nearby objects clearly.

stem: Retina of the eye is comparable to which of the following parts of a traditional camera?
expl: The back of your eye is lined with a layer known as the retina. The retina operates in a similar way to the film inside a traditional (non-digital) camera. The middle part of the retina (known as the macula) takes care of your sharp vision. Your retina's nerve cells change light rays into electrical impulses and then sends them to the brain through the optic nerve.

stem: In human eye, image of object forms at :
expl: The functioning of the human eye is similar to that of the photographic camera. The light rays travel into the cornea are refracted by the cornea and lens. In a normal eye, the image formed are transmitted from the retina to the brain along the optic nerve, where data processing takes place (the image is perceived the right way up).

stem: In long-sightedness, images are formed at following :
expl: In long-sightedness (Hypermetropia) the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina. It results in close objects appearing blurry. The condition occurs in case the eyeball is too short or the focal length of the eye lens has been increased. The long-sightedness is corrected by the convex lens.

stem: The colour of an opaque object is due to the colour it–
expl: The colour of an opaque object is the same as the colour of the light that is reflected by it. Opaque object doesn't pass the light through it. It absorbs some part of incident light and reflects the other part. The reflected part of light decides the colour of that object.

stem: When beams of red, blue and green lights fall on the same spot, the colour of the light becomes :
expl: Red, green and blue are referred to as the primary colours of light. Because we add them together to create a colour, we call them additive colors. Cyan, Magenta and yellow are called the subtractive color because we create colour by using them to subtract colour from white light. If we add all 3 primary colours of light in equal proportions we obtain white colour light.

stem:
Consider the following phenomena :
1. Size of the Sun at dusk
2. Colour of the Sun at dawn
3. Moon being visible at dawn
4. Twinkle of stars in the sky
5. Polestar being visible in the sky
Which of the above are optical illusions?
expl: The size of the Sun at dusk is an optical illusion. The Sun appears smaller during noon but longer at dawn or more clearly at dusk. At dawn, the Sun is seen with other objects on the horizon and looks big. The colour of the Sun at dawn is also an optical illusion. Finally twinkling of stars is also an optical illusion caused by the refraction of light while moving through various layers of atmosphere. Moon being visible at dawn and Polestar being visible in the sky are not optical illusions.
